cases.formatted_markup: {SPEAKER:17}Is it the sail placement...?{LB}No, perhaps...
{SPEAKER:02}Hey! What do you want{LB}with this ship?
{SPEAKER:17}Oh, is this your ship? A little{LB}more work would really improve her.
{SPEAKER:02}??
{SPEAKER:17}Extra sails, perhaps...{LB}or a different basic sail type...
{SPEAKER:02}Um, excuse me...
{SPEAKER:17}More gun batteries{LB}would make her stronger...{LB}Or perhaps a different cannon type{LB}would be better...
{SPEAKER:02}Enough already! Who are you?
{SPEAKER:17}Oh, I'm sorry. I got carried away,{LB}and she's not even my ship...
{SPEAKER:17}I'm Manuel.{LB}I used to be a navigator.
{SPEAKER:02}Navigator, huh...
{SPEAKER:17}Seeing a ship starts me thinking.{LB}Old habits from my days at sea...
{SPEAKER:17}I must seem terribly rude.{LB}I'm sorry. But please, let me say{LB}one last thing.
{SPEAKER:17}This may be none of my business,{LB}but this ship is crying. Please{LB}take better care of her.
{SPEAKER:02}Hey, wait!
{SPEAKER:17}I've spoken out of turn. Please{LB}don't take offense. Well,{LB}I'll be on my way.
{SPEAKER:02}...Odd.
{SPEAKER:09}What do you mean? He is amazing!{LB}{MACRO:FI}, our ship could use{LB}a man like that.
{SPEAKER:02}Why?
{SPEAKER:09}{MACRO:FI}, you never care for the ship.{LB}That is why she is crying.
{SPEAKER:14}And you work us hard.
{SPEAKER:02}What do you expect? I don't know{LB}the first thing about machinery.{LB}I can't help it!
{SPEAKER:09}Don't just shrug it off!{LB}That's why we need someone to love{LB}the ship in {MACRO:FI}'s place.
{SPEAKER:09}Then the ship would stop crying.{LB}May we invite him aboard?
{SPEAKER:02}Hmm... Well, if you're all right{LB}with it, Camille, I suppose{LB}I am too.
{SPEAKER:09}Sir, would you care for our ship?
{SPEAKER:17}You mean become a navigator again?{LB}But it's been so many years{LB}since I left the sea...
{SPEAKER:09}But you should be just as capable{LB}as those of us still at sea.{LB}Someone who loves ships that much{LB}can't have forgotten the sea.
{SPEAKER:17}Well, that is true...
{SPEAKER:09}Then would you take{LB}good care of her?{LB}We seem to make her cry.
{SPEAKER:17}Thank you. If that's how you feel,{LB}I'll do it.
{SPEAKER:17}Once again: Manuel Almeida.{LB}At your service.
{SPEAKER:17}Now then, Admiral. May I offer{LB}some advice on refitting{LB}the flagship's Workrooms?
{SPEAKER:17}Then let us discuss rooms useful{LB}for long-distance voyages.
{SPEAKER:17}Assign officers with high Speech{LB}to the First Mate's Office{LB}or Chapel{LB}to ease the sailors' discontent.
{SPEAKER:17}Staff in the Galley{LB}and Livestock Room{LB}help reduce the fleet's{LB}food and water consumption.
{SPEAKER:17}A Surgeon in the Infirmary treats{LB}fatigue, disease and injuries{LB}among officers and sailors.
{SPEAKER:17}Sick or injured officers{LB}recover faster in a Private Cabin{LB}or Recreation Room.
{SPEAKER:17}A Shipwright like me repairs{LB}damage in the Lumber Room at sea.{LB}I also help refit and repair ships{LB}at shipyards.
{SPEAKER:17}That was a hurried explanation.{LB}Was it useful?
{SPEAKER:17}The fleet's fate{LB}rests on your command.{LB}Be sure to give refitting{LB}the care it deserves.
{SPEAKER:17}I see. I'll leave it to you, then.
